projects.description:
## The problem

Job seekers move between disconnected tools to improve a résumé, evaluate a role, prepare for interviews and track next steps.

## What it does

Prepera brings those steps into one workflow: résumé and job-description analysis, application tracking, AI voice interview practice with an interactive avatar, and salary-negotiation preparation. It supports preparation; it does not promise interviews or offers.

React and TypeScript on Supabase and Postgres, with Claude and OpenAI powering the coaching features.

projects.title: AuthMatch AI
projects.tagline: Decision support for prior-authorization reviewers: matches each case to Medicare coverage policy and shows which criteria the documentation supports.
projects.description:
## The problem

Prior-authorization reviewers have to find the controlling Medicare coverage policy for each case and check the clinical documentation against it by hand. CMS-0057-F sets decision timeframes for this work, including seven calendar days for standard requests and 72 hours for expedited ones.

## What it does

AuthMatch AI matches each case, by procedure code and member state, to the applicable NCD or LCD policy and reads the documentation against it. The reviewer sees each criterion marked Met, Not Met or Indeterminate, with the supporting evidence cited. A qualified human reviewer makes every final decision; the AI never finalizes a case. It is decision support, not a coverage determination or a certification of regulatory compliance.

## Architecture

The Next.js reviewer interface proxies requests and does no PHI processing. Document processing, OCR, policy matching and LLM calls run in a separate FastAPI service. Postgres row-level security restricts data access, and an append-only, hash-chained audit log records case activity.

## Status

MVP. The web and API tiers are deployed.

projects.title: Gen4Me
projects.tagline: Turns a one-line project idea into the CLAUDE.md, PRD, and build plan your AI coding agents need.
projects.description:
## The problem

AI coding agents are only as good as the context you give them, and most projects have stale docs or none at all.

## What it does

From a one-line description of your project, Gen4Me researches your stack on the live web, asks you to confirm its assumptions instead of guessing, and generates a tailored CLAUDE.md, a research-backed PRD, a build plan, and per-directory rules. As the codebase evolves, it audits the docs against the code and flags drift.

## How it's built

Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, and Postgres, with LLM pipelines grounded by live web research.

projects.description:
## The problem

Sanctions lists change often across authorities, and compliance teams usually find out by reading raw regulatory text after the fact.

## What it does

SanctionsWatch collects updates from U.S., U.K., E.U. and U.N. sources on a schedule, deduplicates and classifies them, summarizes the impact with an LLM, and sends alerts. Compliance professionals decide applicability and action.

## Status

Prototype. The public deployment is not currently generating briefings.

## How it's built

Next.js and TypeScript on Supabase and Postgres, with an ingestion pipeline built on Apify.

projects.title: AI Engineering Factory & Analytics
projects.tagline: Built a supervised AI-assisted engineering system that coordinates planning, development, testing, independent review, and human release decisions, alongside a dashboard for delivery evidence and failure analysis.
projects.description:
## The problem

As a solo founder building multiple products, I needed more structured development capacity without losing control over code quality, security, ownership, or the release process.

## The system

I designed a governed workflow in which work is planned, assigned to specialized AI agents, isolated for implementation, checked through automated tests, reviewed independently, and presented for a human decision before release.

## The controls

Scoped task ownership, isolated work environments, security restrictions, testing and review requirements, bounded repair attempts, stop conditions, and recorded execution evidence.

## The analytics

A companion dashboard examines tasks, review outcomes, failures, timing, cost-related records where available, and evidence quality to make engineering performance more visible.

## What this demonstrates

Operating-system design for AI-assisted engineering; agent orchestration; quality governance; engineering metrics; traceability; and iterative improvement.

caseStudy.challenge: As a solo founder building multiple products, I needed more structured development capacity without losing control over code quality, security, ownership, or the release process.
caseStudy.delivered: I designed a governed workflow in which work is planned, assigned to specialized AI agents, isolated for implementation, checked through automated tests, reviewed independently, and presented for a human decision before release. A companion dashboard examines tasks, review outcomes, failures, timing, cost-related records where available, and evidence quality to make engineering performance more visible.
caseStudy.riskAndControls: Scoped task ownership, isolated work environments, security restrictions, testing and review requirements, bounded repair attempts, stop conditions, and recorded execution evidence.
caseStudy.howItWorks:
Every change moves through five phases.

**Govern and intake.** Requests from me, Jira or GitHub issues are reconciled into a ranked queue and revalidated before use. A task is picked only if it is unblocked, unclaimed and within the run budget, with up to three running in parallel.

**Triage and plan.** Work that is ready to build has an approved plan, clear acceptance criteria and bounded scope. Unclear or higher-risk work goes to planner agents, and a person reviews the plan. Missing information or conflicting requests are held for a person, never guessed.

**Build and validate.** One owner claims each task in its own isolated worktree. Specialist agents join only when needed. The implementer works inside the authorized scope and adds regression tests, then the project's quality gates run. Tests are never weakened to get a pass.

**Review and assure.** Independent reviewers run in parallel, chosen by what changed: code, security, AI behavior, UI and accessibility. Blocking findings get at most two repair cycles; then the system stops and asks.

**Approve and learn.** A passing change comes to me for approval before it merges into the protected main branch. Every run is recorded (hashes, not content) and feeds Factory Analytics (lead time, repair rate, review failure rate), which I use to tune the rules and agents.

Governance runs throughout: rules are enforced by hooks, high-risk work needs a person, secrets are scanned, and no agent approves its own work.
caseStudy.role: Designer and sole builder: operating model, agent roles, controls, tooling and analytics
caseStudy.keyDecisions:
- A person approves every change before it merges into the protected main branch; the system cannot merge on its own.
- One owner claims each task, and the work happens in its own isolated worktree, so parallel work cannot collide.
- Reviewers are chosen by what the change touches (code, security, AI behavior, UI and accessibility), not by judgment about whether review is needed.
- Blocking findings get at most two repair cycles; after that the system stops and asks a person.
- Tests are never weakened to obtain a pass.
- Run records store hashes, not content, so analytics never hold source code or prompts.
caseStudy.outcome: The Factory is in use on my own repositories, including the code behind this site. Run records feed Factory Analytics, a local dashboard that reports lead time, repair rate and review failure rate. The recorded sample is still small, so no performance figures are published here, and no claim is made of autonomous delivery or proven productivity gains.

projects.title: Enterprise Technology Operating Model Transformation
projects.tagline: Led the redesign of how JPMorgan Chase Legal Technology organized its global technology portfolio: product definitions, ownership boundaries, decision rights and governance.
projects.description:
## Business challenge

Legal Technology's global technology portfolio, supported by teams in the United States, the United Kingdom and India, had largely been managed as a collection of applications rather than as products. Without clear product definitions and ownership boundaries, it was hard to say where one product ended and another began, who was accountable for each, and which decisions belonged at which level. Accountability, roadmaps and portfolio reviews all depend on clear answers to those questions.

## Leadership responsibility

As Vice President and Chief of Staff for Strategy & Execution, I developed and led the redesign of the product operating model: portfolio rationalization, product boundaries, ownership, governance and decision-right recommendations. I worked with product, technology and business leadership to shape the model and put it into operation.

## Strategic decisions

**From applications to products.** I recommended rationalizing the portfolio into a smaller set of clearly defined products, so each had a coherent scope and an accountable owner.

**A common structure.** I defined a product taxonomy that gave portfolio planning and reviews a consistent structure to work from.

**Decision rights.** I recommended which decisions should sit with product owners and which required portfolio governance or senior leadership.

**Accountability.** I defined the governance responsibilities that held product owners accountable within the new model.

**The central tradeoff.** Moving from an application-centered model to a product-based structure meant balancing consolidation and simplification against keeping product responsibilities, user workflows and decision rights clearly defined. Simplifying the portfolio could not come at the cost of clear ownership, accountability or business alignment.

## Actions and execution

I worked across product, engineering, architecture, UX, site reliability, agility, finance, risk and Legal teams to align roadmaps with the new product structure and to resolve dependencies that crossed product boundaries.

## Organizational impact

Legal Technology moved from managing disconnected applications toward a structured product operating model. Products had defined scopes and owners, decisions had a defined home, and portfolio planning and reviews worked from the same structure.

## Evidence

- A rationalized product portfolio with documented product definitions, ownership boundaries, decision rights and governance responsibilities.
- The resulting model provided a consistent basis for portfolio planning and reviews.

projects.title: Technology Strategy, Portfolio Governance & Business Operations
projects.tagline: Directed the annual strategy and planning cycle that connected Legal Technology's priorities to its roadmap, investment and workforce plans, OKRs and portfolio commitments.
projects.description:
## Business challenge

Legal Technology had to serve competing priorities from Legal, Technology and business partners within investment constraints and finite workforce capacity. Those factors could not be weighed one request at a time: roadmaps, investment plans, staffing and delivery commitments had to rest on the same set of priorities.

## Leadership responsibility

I owned Legal Technology's annual strategy cycle and multi-year roadmap and directed the annual financial planning process. With executive leadership, I established the annual OKR framework. I advised senior leadership on the resulting tradeoffs; the investment decisions were theirs.

## Strategic decisions

**Priorities into commitments.** I translated enterprise Legal, Technology and business priorities into portfolio objectives, product roadmaps, investment decisions, workforce plans and measurable execution commitments.

**One planning view.** I brought competing priorities, investment constraints, workforce capacity and delivery commitments into a single planning view, so leaders could weigh them against each other.

**Alternatives within constraints.** I evaluated investment alternatives against financial constraints and organizational priorities, and set out the tradeoffs for senior leadership.

**Measures that carried through.** I designed OKRs that linked strategic priorities to quarterly outcomes, portfolio commitments and executive performance reviews.

## Actions and execution

Each year I ran the cycle from priority-setting through to commitments: coordinating forecasts, challenging assumptions before they became commitments, aligning roadmaps across teams and resolving the dependencies between them.

## Organizational impact

Roadmaps, investment choices, workforce plans and commitments were set from one agreed set of priorities and measures. The planning outputs informed leadership's investment discussions and, through OKRs and portfolio commitments, became the reference point for overseeing execution during the year.

## Evidence

- An established annual strategy and multi-year planning process connecting executive priorities to product roadmaps, workforce and investment plans, OKRs and portfolio commitments.
- The annual OKR framework, used in quarterly and executive performance reviews.

projects.title: Enterprise AI Strategy & Governance
projects.tagline: Built Legal Technology's AI book of work and the evaluation, governance and measures used to decide which AI opportunities should advance.
projects.description:
## Business challenge

Interest in AI spanned LLM assistants, knowledge and analytics platforms, document automation and AI-enabled legal workflows. The question was not whether to use AI, but which opportunities deserved investment and on what basis. In a legal function, those choices also carried security, privacy, regulatory and AI risk that had to be understood before an initiative advanced.

## Leadership responsibility

I developed and operationalized Legal Technology's AI strategy and directed annual risk, control and privacy readiness for AI/ML-related business cases, including clarifying who was accountable for each.

## Strategic decisions

**Start with the problem.** I evaluated each opportunity from the business problem and the intended outcome, not from the technology.

**Consistent evaluation.** I compared opportunities against a consistent set of considerations: strategic alignment; expected business value and process improvement; technical feasibility and complexity; the availability, reliability and appropriateness of data; security, privacy, regulatory and AI risk; cost and resource requirements; user adoption and operational readiness; and whether the intended value could be measured.

**One book of work.** I managed AI opportunities as one book of work, so they were prioritized against each other and against the rest of the portfolio.

**Value after launch.** I defined adoption and ROI measures, so initiatives were assessed on whether the intended value was realized.

## Actions and execution

I worked with risk, privacy, Legal, product and engineering partners to take AI/ML business cases through governance, re-attestation, assessment and remediation, and reported AI progress to senior leadership as part of executive reporting. The evaluation informed use-case prioritization, roadmap planning, governance and investment discussions.

## Organizational impact

Legal Technology gained a structured way to evaluate AI opportunities and assess their readiness before advancing them, with prioritization, accountability and value measures built into portfolio and executive reviews.

## Evidence

- An AI book of work with defined evaluation considerations, prioritization, governance responsibilities, and adoption and value measures.
- Those measures incorporated into portfolio and executive review processes.
- Governance, re-attestation, assessment and remediation activities for AI/ML-related business cases.

projects.title: Executive Decision Support & Performance Management
projects.tagline: Built the executive operating rhythm that turned portfolio, financial, workforce and risk information into decisions for Legal Technology's senior leaders.
projects.description:
## Business challenge

Senior leaders needed consistent visibility into portfolio commitments, operational performance, financial and workforce considerations, risks, and decisions requiring intervention. That information came from product, engineering, finance and workforce teams, and it had to be turned into something leaders could act on.

## Leadership responsibility

I prepared executive strategy materials, portfolio analyses and decision-support information for senior Legal and Technology leadership, including materials used in General Counsel briefings, and organized the management reviews where that information was discussed.

## Strategic decisions

**What leaders needed to see.** I structured strategy presentations, quarterly business reviews, monthly operating reviews and portfolio dashboards around commitments, performance, financial and workforce position, risks and open decisions.

**From information to decisions.** I organized each review around the decisions that required leadership intervention, the tradeoffs involved and the issues to escalate.

**Challenge before escalation.** I challenged assumptions and clarified issues with teams before material went to senior leadership.

## Actions and execution

I connected information across product, engineering, finance and workforce teams, reported performance against OKRs, supported escalation and corrective-action discussions in monthly operating reviews, and wrote the financial analyses and executive narratives that framed each decision.

## Organizational impact

Portfolio progress, resource considerations, risks and decisions came into one leadership review process. Leaders reviewed priorities, commitments and required actions in a consistent structure, and the reviews supported prioritization and corrective decisions.

## Evidence

- A recurring executive operating rhythm: strategy presentations, quarterly business reviews, monthly operating reviews, portfolio dashboards and performance reporting.
- Decision-support materials for senior Legal and Technology leadership, including materials used in General Counsel briefings.

projects.title: Workforce Strategy, Talent Development & Organizational Planning
projects.tagline: Directed the annual workforce planning that reconciled demand for technology delivery with capacity, location and investment constraints, and supported early-career technical talent.
projects.description:
## Business challenge

Technology priorities had to be reconciled with workforce capacity, staffing constraints, hiring requirements, location considerations, attrition and talent development. Across a global organization, the demand for delivery and the capacity to meet it had to be planned together.

## Leadership responsibility

I directed the annual financial and workforce planning process within Legal Technology. I advised leadership on capacity, hiring, location strategy and investment tradeoffs, and supported their decisions on staffing, location and hiring, which required senior approval.

## Strategic decisions

**Demand against capacity.** I aligned workforce requirements with product priorities and evaluated capacity before demand became a commitment.

**Scenarios, not a single answer.** I developed staffing, location and investment scenarios, including constrained-budget scenarios, focused on prioritization, capacity and where resources should be reallocated.

**Assumptions tested.** I challenged forecast assumptions before they shaped the plan.

**Guardrails.** I developed and recommended workforce planning guardrails for leadership consideration.

## Actions and execution

I coordinated hiring and attrition forecasts and connected the workforce plan to the financial plan and the roadmap. I also supported early-career software engineering recruitment, engineering onboarding and mentoring, and the development of emerging technical talent.

## Organizational impact

One annual process connected product demand, staffing forecasts, capacity, hiring plans, location considerations and investment constraints. It gave senior leadership a structured basis for workforce decisions.

## Evidence

- An annual workforce planning process connecting product demand, staffing forecasts, capacity, hiring plans, location considerations and investment constraints.
- Involvement in early-career technical recruitment, onboarding and talent development.

projects.title: PMO Leadership & Cross-Functional Delivery Governance
projects.tagline: Led the PMO and business-analysis team and the delivery governance that helped leaders assess commitments, identify delivery issues and coordinate corrective action.
projects.description:
## Business challenge

Multiple initiatives required coordinated delivery governance, consistent accountability, escalation mechanisms, dependency management and performance oversight across product and engineering teams.

## Leadership responsibility

I led the PMO and business-analysis team of project managers, Scrum Masters and business analysts. Beyond that team I worked through influence: delivery stayed with product and engineering leaders, and my role was the governance they delivered within. I also directed annual risk, control and privacy readiness and oversaw corrective actions.

## Strategic decisions

**Consistent standards.** I coordinated planning and delivery standards across initiatives, so commitments, status and risks were reported on the same basis.

**Escalation.** I supported escalation practices that brought delivery risks to the leaders who needed to act on them.

**Reporting for decisions.** I improved management reporting so commitments, dependencies and emerging risks were visible together.

## Actions and execution

I directed the team's work, worked with product and engineering stakeholders to manage commitments, tracked dependencies across teams and coordinated corrective actions.

## Organizational impact

Leaders had clearer delivery oversight, more consistent governance across initiatives and better visibility into execution risks and dependencies. They used it to assess commitments, identify delivery issues and coordinate corrective action.

## Evidence

- A PMO governance approach with consistent planning standards, portfolio reporting, delivery oversight, dependency tracking, escalation practices and executive decision support.
- Annual risk, control and privacy readiness, and corrective-action oversight.

projects.title: JPMorgan Chase: Legal Technology Strategy & Transformation
projects.tagline: Connected business priorities to technology strategy, product governance, multi-year roadmaps, financial and workforce planning, and executive decision-making across a global Legal Technology organization.
projects.description:
## The challenge

In Legal Technology, the challenge is not simply delivering isolated projects. It is aligning different product areas, technical teams, business partners, resources, and control obligations around a coherent set of priorities. I led the management processes that helped translate those priorities into plans, ownership, governance, and delivery accountability.

## My contribution

Annual strategy cycle, portfolio and roadmap alignment, financial and workforce planning, organizational operating-model improvements, executive reviews, and AI opportunity prioritization.

Helped establish clearer priorities, accountability, and decision-making across the technology portfolio.

about.name: Erick Clark
about.title: Technology Strategy & AI Transformation Professional
about.heroTagline: Former Vice President and Chief of Staff for Legal Technology at JPMorgan Chase who also designs and builds working AI products. I understand technology from the executive decision to the working product.
bio: I understand technology from the executive decision to the working product. For more than 15 years I have worked on both sides of that line: deciding what an organization should invest in, and making sure what it builds actually works.

It started in the U.S. Army, where I served as an intelligence analyst. I turned complex, incomplete information into assessments and briefings that supported senior leaders' decisions, and I supervised and developed junior analysts. Clear analysis that ends in a clear recommendation still shapes how I work.

I then spent several years delivering technology in energy and technology services, at CenterPoint Energy, NRG Energy and CSAT Solutions: network infrastructure programs, billing and payment platforms, PMO governance and automation. Delivery taught me what a plan looks like once it meets engineering, vendors and operations.

At JPMorgan Chase, as Vice President and Chief of Staff for Legal Technology from 2019 to 2026, I worked on the decisions that shape delivery. I owned the annual strategy cycle and multi-year roadmap, led the redesign of the product operating model, directed financial and workforce planning, built the executive reporting for the General Counsel and senior Technology leadership, and developed the organization's AI strategy and governance model.

Since 2024 I have also designed and built AI products independently: AuthMatch AI for prior-authorization review, Prepera for career preparation, regulatory-monitoring tools, and a supervised AI engineering system that runs my own software delivery. Building them shows me where AI initiatives succeed or stall: data quality, controls, human review and the cost of operating them.
That combination is what I bring to a leadership role. I can set the strategy, govern the investment, and work credibly with the people building it.

I hold an MBA, an M.S. in Management Information Systems and a B.S. in Business & Accounting, with PMP, Professional Scrum Master, AWS Cloud Practitioner and FinOps certifications. The fastest way to reach me is email.
about.quote: I’ve never been satisfied with just understanding how something works. I want to know how to make it better.

experience.description: Design and build AI products independently, from product strategy and architecture through implementation and deployment: AuthMatch AI (prior-authorization review support), Prepera (career preparation), SanctionsWatch and a regulatory intelligence platform (regulatory monitoring), Gen4Me, and a supervised AI engineering system. Every product keeps a human decision-maker in the loop.

experience.role: VP, Chief of Staff (Strategy & Execution), Legal Technology
experience.description: Owned Legal Technology's annual strategy cycle and multi-year roadmap and directed annual financial and workforce planning across a global technology portfolio. Led the redesign of the product operating model, developed and operationalized the AI strategy and governance model, and prepared executive strategy materials and decision support for senior Legal and Technology leadership.

Senior PMO business partner for Apple and Dell technology programs. Shipped an automated, NIST 800-88 compliant data-deletion solution for decommissioned government laptops that cut human error by 90%, and led automation and modernization initiatives worth about $5M in annual savings.

Led delivery of retail-energy platforms across business, technology, compliance, and vendor teams. SAP billing enhancements cut annual operating costs by $500K, and a PCI-compliant IVR payment system expanded secure self-service while reducing average call-handling time by 20%.
Led the $29.4M fiber expansion program, improving communications throughput by 40%, and governed $8M in capital-project budgets across engineering, operations, vendors, and field teams.

Produced predictive intelligence assessments and delivered classified briefings to senior leaders, translating complex findings into clear recommended actions. Supervised and developed junior analysts.

it.h1: I turn enterprise technology priorities into decisions, delivery, and results.
it.body: I'm a former JPMorgan Chase Vice President and Chief of Staff with more than 15 years of experience across technology strategy, enterprise transformation, portfolio governance, and business operations. I also design and build AI-powered products, giving me direct experience connecting executive decisions to technical execution.

consultant.h1: I help organizations turn complex business problems into practical technology solutions.
consultant.body: I work across business strategy, operations, AI, and technology to understand what's slowing an organization down, identify opportunities, and define a realistic path forward. My approach combines executive-level planning with hands-on delivery experience, so recommendations account for what it actually takes to implement them.

builder.h1: I turn ideas into working software that solves real problems.
builder.body: I design and develop AI-powered applications, business platforms, and automation systems. My work spans product strategy, architecture, databases, integrations, AI workflows, testing, and deployment. I use AI-assisted engineering with defined quality and security controls while retaining human judgment over important decisions.

capabilitiesHead.heading: Different roles. A connected set of capabilities.
capabilitiesHead.lede: My experience spans the decisions that shape technology, the operating systems that deliver it, and the products that make it tangible.

it.title: Technology Strategy
it.body: I translate business priorities into technology objectives, investment decisions, multi-year roadmaps, and measurable outcomes. My experience includes annual strategy cycles and leadership alignment across complex technology organizations.

it.title: Enterprise Transformation
it.body: I help organizations redesign operating models, clarify product ownership, improve decision rights, and manage the changes required to make transformation sustainable.

it.title: AI Strategy
it.body: I identify and prioritize AI opportunities based on business value, feasibility, cost, adoption requirements, and risk. My experience spans enterprise AI planning and independent product development.

it.title: Portfolio & Investment Governance
it.body: I establish planning, prioritization, dependencies, reporting, and decision processes that help organizations deliver important initiatives.

it.title: Technology Business Operations
it.body: I connect strategy to financial planning, workforce capacity, vendor management, resource allocation, operating reviews, and performance management.

it.title: AI Governance
it.body: I apply governance principles to AI systems, including risk assessment, accountability, data protection, human oversight, evaluation, and monitoring. My product work provides practical implementation experience.

it.title: Executive Leadership & Reporting
it.body: I work across technology, finance, risk, operations, and senior leadership to communicate tradeoffs, resolve competing priorities, and translate complex issues into clear decisions.

consultant.title: Business Discovery
consultant.body: I examine how an organization operates, where work gets delayed, and what problems actually need solving before recommending technology.

consultant.title: Process Redesign
consultant.body: I simplify manual workflows, reduce unnecessary handoffs, and identify opportunities for automation and better information flow.

consultant.title: AI Opportunity Assessment
consultant.body: I identify where AI could improve productivity, decision support, customer experience, and operations while considering data readiness, costs, and risks.

consultant.title: Strategy & Roadmapping
consultant.body: I help leaders define the desired outcome, evaluate alternatives, prioritize investments, and create an achievable implementation roadmap.

consultant.title: Risk & Governance
consultant.body: I help organizations think through AI controls, privacy, accountability, human approval, security requirements, and operational risk.

consultant.title: Implementation Advisory
consultant.body: I connect recommendations to execution through requirements, solution planning, technical coordination, delivery oversight, and hands-on implementation where appropriate.

consultant.title: Adoption & Enablement
consultant.body: I help teams understand tools, adapt workflows, establish ownership, and develop skills to operate and improve solutions after launch.

builder.title: Product Strategy
builder.body: I translate business problems into product requirements, user journeys, priorities, and incremental releases.

builder.title: UX & Product Design
builder.body: I shape user journeys, interface structure, and administrative workflows so products are clear to use, then refine them with feedback before and after release.

builder.title: Web & App Development
builder.body: I develop web applications and business platforms with user authentication, databases, interfaces, integrations, and administrative workflows.

builder.title: Data & Integrations
builder.body: I design data models and connect applications to APIs, external services, business processes, and information sources.

builder.title: AI Engineering & Automation
builder.body: I build AI-powered features using language models, retrieval, specialized agents, structured workflows, and human review.

builder.title: Security & Quality
builder.body: I incorporate access controls, data boundaries, validation, testing, auditability, and risk-based approval into software delivery.

builder.title: Deployment & Improvement
builder.body: I take applications through testing and deployment, then use monitoring, feedback, and operational evidence to guide improvements.

approach.heading: From understanding the problem to delivering the outcome.
approach.intro: The technology is never the starting point. The business problem is.

steps.title: Understand the problem
steps.body: I start by learning the business, its users, workflows, constraints, costs, and current challenges. I distinguish the original request from the underlying problem and identify what success should look like.

steps.title: Define the right approach
steps.body: I evaluate possible solutions, challenge assumptions, prioritize opportunities, and establish requirements, ownership, risks, dependencies, and measures of success.

steps.title: Deliver, measure, and improve
steps.body: I connect the plan to implementation. Depending on the engagement, that may mean leading an enterprise initiative, advising a delivery team, or personally developing a product. I focus on adoption, reliability, and evidence of business value.

work.heading: Experience that connects strategy to execution.
work.intro: My work includes enterprise technology leadership, paid client delivery, and independent software products. Each demonstrates a different part of how I frame problems, make decisions, and deliver outcomes.

pointOfView.heading: Technology only counts when it ships, holds up under scrutiny, and leaves people more capable.

principles.title: Business outcomes before technology
principles.body: I believe every technology initiative should begin with a clearly defined problem, an accountable owner, and a way to determine whether the investment was worthwhile.

principles.title: Governance belongs in delivery
principles.body: Security, risk, data protection, and human accountability should influence how a solution is designed and implemented, not become a final checklist before launch.

principles.title: Execution proves the strategy
principles.body: A compelling presentation is not a business outcome. The real test is whether people adopt the solution, operations improve, and the organization can sustain the result.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: How the contact form and analytics on this site handle your information. Last updated October 26, 2026.

sections.title: Who operates this site
paragraphs: This site is operated by Erick Clark.

sections.title: What the contact form collects
paragraphs: Your name and email address, the type of inquiry you choose, and your answers to that inquiry type's questions. Depending on the type, these can include your organization, role or project details, links you add, budget, timeframe and similar business details you choose to enter.
Each message also includes the inquiry type, the page you sent it from, the audience view you were reading, the time it was received, and the version of the privacy acknowledgment you accepted.
The site does not store submissions in a database. Each one is sent as an email, and the message then exists in the recipient's mailbox and with the email provider.

sections.title: How your information is used and where it goes
paragraphs: To understand your request and reply to it, using the email address you provide.

Leadership opportunity, product or partnership, and general inquiries go to Erick directly. Strategic advisory, build-a-product, and speaking or training inquiries go to a business inbox for Clark Strategic Systems LLC. Commercial inquiries of these kinds may be handled through Clark Strategic Systems LLC.

sections.title: Service providers
paragraphs: Contact form messages are delivered by email through Resend.

To limit abuse, the form keeps short-lived counters in a Redis database. Counters are keyed to a one-way hash of your IP address, not the address itself. The form also uses a hidden field and a minimum-time check to filter automated submissions.
The site is hosted on Vercel.

sections.title: Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: The site includes Vercel Web Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights to measure aggregate traffic and page performance. Vercel documents that Web Analytics uses no third-party cookies and identifies visitors by a hash created from the incoming request, and that Speed Insights data is not tied to an individual visitor or IP address. Data points include page URL, referrer, approximate location, browser, operating system and device type.
The site itself does not set cookies for visitors. A sign-in cookie exists only for the site owner's administrative area.

sections.title: Health and sensitive information
paragraphs: The contact form does not ask for health information. Please do not include protected health information, passwords, government IDs or confidential business documents in a message.

sections.title: How long information is kept
paragraphs: Messages are kept while we are in conversation and deleted within 90 days after it ends, unless they lead to a working relationship.
The form's abuse-prevention counters expire on their own within 10 minutes (per visitor) and 24 hours (site-wide). Analytics data is kept under Vercel's retention policy.

sections.title: Visitors outside the United States
paragraphs: Your message is used because you asked for a reply, which is a legitimate interest in answering it. The service providers named above may process it in the United States.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Reasonable technical measures protect the site and its messages. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: This site is for professional inquiries and is not directed to children under 13.

sections.title: Your choices and requests
paragraphs: You can ask what you have sent through this site, ask for a correction, or ask for deletion by emailing {email}. Requests are answered within 30 days.
Your information is never sold or shared for advertising.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: Updates are posted on this page with a new date.
